subject: Post-call: data lifecycle options & trace masking — Acme Health
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: data lifecycle options & trace masking — Acme Health

Thanks again for your time this morning, Sanjay — appreciate the detailed run-through of the CareAssist pilot goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Ask: Acme needs assurance that PII is not stored beyond what’s strictly necessary for model context and troubleshooting. Main concerns are: indirect identifiers in session traces and compliance for pre-auth patient data.
- What we covered: Redwood can offer configurable session trace handling (masked/hashing at ingest), a hashed-only troubleshooting bundle, and a private deployment option if you need network isolation.
- Proposal (quick take): two options for pilot:
  1) Transient session traces: retain hashed traces (no raw texts) for 14 days for debugging; KV / context caches not persisted to disk beyond 24 hours.
  2) Locked-down pilot: private deployment (VPC) + disabled trace collection; longer lead time and higher cost.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I’ll circulate a short SLA addendum and security evidence bundle for option (1) — Marissa is looping in security evidence.
2) Sanjay / Legal to flag any must-have language (e.g., absolute deletion clauses, audit windows).
3) We aim to finalize pilot config and SOW by next Friday (2026-11-12) to hit a Dec pilot start.

Attachments: SLA-draft-acmehealth.pdf (initial addendum), security-evidence-2026.zip (SOC2 summary, encryption notes)

Cheers,

— Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@acmehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: data lifecycle options & trace masking — Acme Health

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

1) When you say "hashed traces" — will the hashes be reversible by Redwood? We need cryptographic one-way hashing for any patient identifiers.
2) Who has access to the hashed troubleshooting bundle? Can access be limited to named engineers with audited access?
3) For the KV/context cache retention (24 hours) — any possibility to reduce that to 6–12 hours for the pilot? Our compliance team is asking for the shortest possible window.

Also our legal team would like to see the precise text for the deletion guarantee and any exceptions (e.g., law enforcement). I’ll loop Legal once we have the draft.

Thanks — Sanjay
Sanjay Reddy
Director of AI Platforms, Acme Health
sanjay.reddy@acmehealth.com

From: Legal Team <legal@acmehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: data lifecycle options & trace masking — Acme Health

Lauren / Rishi — attaching high level redlines and two carve requests from our privacy team. Key asks: 

- Deletion guarantee: require explicit certification within 10 business days after request that all copies of specified data (including hashed troubleshooting bundles) are destroyed.
- Access controls: named-admin access only; require monthly access review reports.
- Cache window: proposed maximum 12 hours for context/KV cache during pilot.

We are OK with hashed-only troubleshooting bundles provided the hashing uses a one-way salt + rotating key per customer and you confirm that Redwood engineering cannot map hashes back to raw inputs.

See attached: ACME_Redlines_v1.pdf

— Acme Legal
legal@acmehealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@acmehealth.com>, Legal Team <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: data lifecycle options & trace masking — Acme Health

Sanjay / Acme Legal — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Short answers and commitments from Redwood Security/Privacy: 

- Hashing: we will implement customer-scoped HMAC (SHA-256) with a per-customer rotating salt; keys are stored in your dedicated KMS namespace when on Dedicated/Private, otherwise in our KMS with CMK separation. Hashes are one-way; Redwood will not retain the raw pre-hash payloads beyond the stated cache window.
- Access: access to troubleshooting bundles will be role-based and require explicit named-engineer approval; we can provide monthly access logs as requested.
- Cache window: we can meet a 12-hour maximum KV/context cache window for the pilot if you accept the default 14-day hashed-trace window for debug artifacts.
- Deletion certification: we can provide certification within 10 business days after a verified request; exceptions for lawful process apply and will be spelled out in the addendum.

Action items:
1) Lauren / Marissa to share updated SLA addendum reflecting the 12-hour cache window and 14-day hashed trace, plus the deletion-cert language.
2) Lauren to coordinate a short technical call next week (30 minutes) so our engineers can walk Acme through the hashing and access controls.

I’ll stand by for the SOW draft.

— Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
